title: SALSA: Sampling Adversarial Suffixes from Learned Distributions for LLM Safety Assessment
abstract: arXiv:2611.33030v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, where adversaries append optimized suffixes to otherwise benign looking prompts to bypass safety alignment. Existing optimization-based GCG-style attacks can be effective, but they are expensive at inference time, and suffer from poor transfer. We present, SALSA, a generative framework that learns a distribution over jailbreak suffixes from optimization-derived attack corpora. Once trained, the model supports efficient sampling-based attacks. On open-source targets, it achieves attack success rates comparable to state-of-the-art optimization baselines, while reducing generation time from 3.46s to 0.04s per prompt. In black-box transfer, it remains highly effective against proprietary systems, including 99% ASR on GPT-3.5-Turbo, and reaches 45% ASR on the substantially harder GPT-4o, more than doubling the strongest baseline at an equal sampling budget. translated_title: SALSA：从学习到的分布中采样对抗性后缀以评估大语言模型安全性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）仍然容易受到越狱攻击的威胁，攻击者在看似无害的提示后面附加经过优化的后缀，从而绕过安全对齐。现有的基于优化的GCG类攻击虽然有效，但在推理时代价高昂，且迁移能力较差。我们提出了SALSA，一个生成式框架，它从基于优化生成的攻击语料库中学习越狱后缀的分布。训练完成后，该模型能够支持高效的基于采样的攻击。在开源目标模型上，它取得了与最先进的优化基线相当的攻击成功率，同时将每个提示的生成时间从3.46秒降至0.04秒。在黑盒迁移场景中，它对专有系统仍然非常有效，包括在GPT-3.5-Turbo上达到99%的攻击成功率（ASR），并在难度显著更高的GPT-4o上达到45%的ASR，在相同采样预算下是最强基线的两倍以上。
tldr: SALSA提出了一种从优化攻击语料中学习越狱后缀分布的生成式框架，在将生成速度提升约90倍的同时达到与最先进优化攻击相当的成功率，并在黑盒迁移中对GPT-3.5-Turbo和GPT-4o分别实现99%和45%的攻击成功率。
en_tdlr: SALSA is a generative framework that learns distributions over jailbreak suffixes for efficient sampling-based attacks, matching state-of-the-art optimization baselines with ~90x speedup while achieving strong black-box transfer with 99% ASR on GPT-3.5-Turbo and 45% ASR on GPT-4o.
